THE "NOTHING EXISTS" CLAIM IS VERIFIED, not assumed, and here is exactly what was checked so the next reader knows the scope of the sweep: (a) case-insensitive grep for `slide` across `src/`, `modules/skai-gaming/src/` and `supabase/` returns 454+148+5 hits and EVERY SINGLE ONE is a false positive - they are `slider` (the Dice and Hi-Lo win-chance sliders: game-settlement/index.ts:1271 "Stake-style slider", points-game/index.ts:5379-5381, gameCanonParams.ts:83, gameSettlementService.ts:1996, pointsGameAdapter.ts:464-466, migration 20260430100500:37) or motion/CSS prose ("the composer slides down", "slide-in from the right", `animate-slide`, `motionPresets.ts:53`). There is not one occurrence of `slide` as a game identifier. (b) No `/play/slide` route - App.tsx registers 12 game routes (:1333-1501) and Slide is not among them. (c) Not in the Play.tsx tile catalog - 24 game tiles at :222-521, no slide. (d) No settlement type: gameSettlementService.ts's game-type map has a `limbo: 'limbo'` entry (:494) but no slide; gameCanonParams.ts's unsupported list (:170-171) names blackjack/crash/tower/chicken/rps/skaicross/poker/limbo/price_grid and not slide. (e) No normalization entry - gameTypeNormalization.ts has no slide branch. (f) LIVE DB CHECKED, not just the repo: `site_config` has zero rows whose key or value matches slide; `feature_flags` has zero rows matching slide/carousel; the daily-loss-cap seed (migration 20260430100500:35-52) enumerates 18 game types and slide is absent; and `game_history`/`game_settlements`/`pool_participants` contain only blackjack, crash_live, hilo, plinko, sports_bet, vegasslots. ★ SO THE STATEMENT IS THE STRONG ONE: not "I could not find it" but "it is not there" - the registries that a game MUST appear in were each enumerated and each came back complete-without-slide. Slide is strictly emptier than Limbo, which at least owns a settlement-type string. ||| FRAME INVENTORY - 13 REAL / 4 SCAFFOLDING, and Slide is the RICHEST of the four new pages: it has ZERO raw `Screenshot 2026-*` leaves and ZERO childless rounded-rectangle placeholders, unlike Crash whose own page carries two raw screenshots (10120-3087/3088). The two default-named `Frame 1000004128/9` nodes are the ONLY ones that look like scaffolding by name and are NOT - one is the cover art and one is the reel sketch, both real design content, both correctly typed `non-screen` in the registry. ||| ★★★ WHAT THE GAME IS - THE FRAMES ANSWER THIS THEMSELVES, IN WRITING. Both assembled pages carry the game's own description as body copy (10030-41378 and 10117-44627, the "Slide / Skai Originals" block): "Pick your target and watch the multipliers roll. The carousel slides through multipliers and stops on one, and if it lands at or above the number you called, you get paid. One round, one landing, and everyone's watching the same slide." That is not inference from pixels, it is the designer stating the mechanic. The board render (10030-42256) confirms every clause: a horizontal reel of multiplier cards, each card 110x230 on a 118px pitch, inside a 1413.7px-wide strip positioned at x=-271 within a 954px clipping frame - i.e. an OVERFLOW-HIDDEN reel wider than its viewport, which is what makes it slide; a FIXED WHITE VERTICAL NEEDLE with a ball terminal anchored at the horizontal centre, which the reel travels beneath; the card currently under the needle (6.33x) rendered LARGER than its neighbours (115.7x242 vs 110x230), lifted into a cyan-bordered filled state with a downward chevron notch - the landing card; cards fading out toward both edges via an edge mask; a colour-TIERED cap bar on each card and a matching colour scale in the history strip above (100.92x green, 99.99x and 10.00x amber, 9.99x and 5.00x cyan, 4.99x and 2.00x white, 1.99x neutral), so multiplier magnitude drives colour; and a bottom status bar reading "Participants: 120" behind a live green dot on the left, "Next round in: 4.2s" on the right, over a full-width teal countdown progress bar. SO: SLIDE IS LIMBO'S MATH ON CRASH'S SHARED-ROUND RAILS, PRESENTED AS A CSGO-CASE-OPENING / HORIZONTAL-SPINNER REEL. The player pre-commits a target multiplier before the round; one shared roll resolves for everybody at once; win iff landed >= target; payout at the target, not at the landed value (that is the standard Limbo construction and is the only one consistent with "if it lands AT OR ABOVE the number you called"). NEAREST SIBLING TO FORK: crash/ - and the vocabulary match is not a coincidence, Slide's frame set (Extended LB, Auto, Auto Advanced, LB With Header, Mobile, Mobile Extended LB, Mobile Auto, Mobile Auto Advanced) is a one-for-one reproduction of Crash's page (9137-13564, 9142-16809, 9142-19197, 9142-19454, 9156-1198, 9156-1371, 9156-1558). WHAT DIFFERS FROM CRASH: Crash's multiplier RISES CONTINUOUSLY and the player's decision is WHEN TO CASH OUT mid-round; Slide has no during-round decision at all - the target is locked before the reel moves and there is exactly one landing. That removes the cash-out button, the live rising-multiplier animation, the per-player cashout ledger and the abandoned-round sweep, and replaces them with a single deterministic landing value per round. WHAT DIFFERS FROM instant/: the instant/ games (Dice, Plinko, RPS) are single-player and resolve per-request; Slide has "Participants: 128" and "Next round in: 4.2s", so it needs a shared round lifecycle that instant/ has no machinery for. ||| ★★★ THE ONE THING THAT BLOCKS A BUILD, AND IT IS A CASEY DECISION, NOT AN ENGINEERING ONE - THE FRAMES CONTRADICT EACH OTHER ON THE CORE MECHANIC. The two ASSEMBLED pages (10030-41378, 10117-44627) label the field "Target Multiplier:" with value 2.00, which matches the description copy and the pre-commit reading above. But ALL FIVE standalone panel variants label the SAME field "Auto Cashout:" - 10030-42281, 10030-42410, 10030-42517, 10117-46093, 10117-46223, 10117-46330. "Auto Cashout" is Crash's label and implies a cash-out-during-round mechanic; "Target Multiplier" implies a pre-committed bet that cannot be exited. These are different games with different risk profiles, different house-edge formulas and different settlement shapes. The most probable reading is that the panel variants were duplicated from Crash's panel and only the assembled pages were re-labelled, so "Target Multiplier" is the intent and "Auto Cashout" is copy-paste debris - but that is a GUESS, and it is a guess about a money path, so it must be Casey's call before a line is written. DO NOT resolve it by picking the label that appears more often. ||| ★★★ ODDS AND MULTIPLIERS IN THESE FRAMES ARE DESIGN CONTENT AND ARE NOT A SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR MONEY. Recorded here so nobody mistakes them for a paytable: the reel cards read 1.22x, 1.22x, 1.22x, 1.22x, 10.22x, 5.01x, 6.33x, 1.22x, 2.00x, 102.23x, 1.22x, 1.22x; the history strip reads 1.99x, 1.99x, 1.99x, 1.99x, 100.92x, 99.99x, 10.00x, 9.99x, 5.00x, 4.99x, 2.00x, 1.99x; the panels show "Potential Profit: (4.20x)" alongside a target of 2.00 (internally inconsistent - 4.20x does not follow from 2.00), a balance of "100.11 SKAI / $21.00" on some panels and "100.11 USDC / $1.00" on the desktop page, and 20 identical live-bet rows of "2.340195". The history values are pseudo-pairs (100.92/99.99, 10.00/9.99, 5.00/4.99, 2.00/1.99) - a designer filling a row with plausible-looking numbers, not a sampled distribution - and seven of twelve reel cards being exactly 1.22x is not a Limbo distribution either. ★ THIS IS THE KENO LESSON: Keno's frames were found printing payouts matching no row of the real server table. There is a "Provably fair" chip and the line "Every game result can be verified using verified" (sic, truncated copy) but NO seed/nonce/verify UI is drawn, so the commit-reveal surface is undesigned. ||| ⚠ TWO FRAMES ARE DUPLICATED PAGE TEMPLATES NAMED FOR THE WRONG GAME - both are REAL screens with genuine Slide content, and the misleading NAME must not be allowed to corrupt the mechanics read. 10030-41378 is named "Skai > Play > Casino > Towers (1440 x 900px)" and 10117-44627 is named "Skai > Play > Casino > Blackjack (375 x 812px)"; both were duplicated from those games' pages and never renamed. Their CONTENT is unambiguously Slide - both contain the "Slide / Skai Originals" heading, the carousel description copy, "Target Multiplier:", "Participants: 128" and "Next round in: 4.2s". Those are template debris, not Slide requirements. ||| BUILD ESTIMATE AND THE SHAPE OF THE WORK. Forking Crash is the right move for the page and the panel and the WRONG move for the engine. The Crash surface is ~7,950 lines across five files (AviatorGamePro.tsx 5,167, crashLiveRoundService.ts 919, crashMultiplayerService.ts 490, CrashPageSections.tsx 1,111, crashPageContent.ts 262). Reusable near-verbatim: the whole page scaffold (CrashPageSections + crashPageContent -> SlidePageSections + slidePageContent), the entire bet panel including Manual/Auto tabs, 1/2 - 2X - Max chips, the Auto block and the On Win / On Loss / Increase By / Stop on Win / Stop on Loss ladder (Slide's 10030-42517 and 10117-46330 draw these identically to Crash's), the live-bets card, the history strip, and the shared-round lifecycle scaffolding in crashLiveRoundService (countdown, participants count, round open/close). Genuinely NEW and not forkable: the reel component itself - a clipped overflow strip, a deterministic easing curve that must land the correct card exactly under a fixed centre needle, the enlarge/highlight transition on the landing card, the edge fade mask, and the multiplier-to-colour tier scale; plus the server-side round engine (a per-round landing multiplier drawn from a declared distribution, provably-fair commit-reveal, and settlement). ROUGH SIZE: front end ~1.5-2.5k lines (page + panel are mostly a fork; the reel is the real work), server ~400-700 lines, plus the registration tax every game pays - App.tsx route, Play.tsx tile, gameTypeNormalization entry, gameSettlementService type, a `site_config` max-bet row (see the 9-games-frozen-at-defaults finding), a daily-loss-cap row, and a feature flag. ★ THE ANIMATION IS A CORRECTNESS SURFACE, NOT A POLISH SURFACE: the reel must be driven BY the settled result, never the result read off where the animation stopped, or the display and the ledger will disagree exactly the way Crash's 100x display cap already does. ||| OPEN QUESTIONS FOR CASEY, in the order that unblocks the most work: (1) Target Multiplier or Auto Cashout - is the target locked before the round, or can a player exit mid-slide? Everything else depends on this. (2) What is the landing distribution and the house edge? If it is Limbo-standard the server draws result = (1-edge)/U and pays the target, but the edge is undeclared and no frame states one. (3) Are the reel cards a FIXED finite set the wheel is built from, or a continuous draw merely rendered as cards? The frames show 12 cards including a 102.23x, which reads continuous, but a fixed set is a different game and a different max-win exposure. (4) Shared round or per-player? "Participants: 128" and "everyone's watching the same slide" say shared, which is materially more infrastructure than an instant game. (5) Which currency rails at launch - the panels disagree between SKAI and USDC, and per the standing gates the sUSD relays and real-money play are their own decision. (6) Max win / max bet caps, given a 102.23x is drawn on the board. NOTHING SHOULD BE BUILT UNTIL (1) AND (2) ARE ANSWERED - they are the mechanic and the money, and every frame below them is already specified well enough to fork.
